title: Accrue interest on every balance before the report reads them

blocks.text: At month end the bank adds interest to every account. The balances, in cents, sit in one `long[]` of a few million entries, and `Accrual` adjusts them in place on a `ForkJoinPool`. The month-end report reads the array the moment `accrue()` returns. On the test book of thirty accounts the report is always right; on the real one, auditors find accounts with no interest and accounts that got it twice.
Finish `compute()` of the `Adjust` task in `src/main/java/practice/Accrual.java`. `adjustHere()` already adjusts a task's own range on the current thread. When you're done:

items: a range of up to `threshold` balances is adjusted by its own task;
a longer range is adjusted by several of the pool's workers at once;
on a book of any size, every balance gets exactly one month of interest;
when `accrue()` returns, the report sees every balance adjusted.

blocks.text: About seven lines in total. The tests run `Accrual` on real pools of two and three workers, and one test holds a single account's adjustment for a while.

cases.says: a book of balances no longer than the threshold, including an empty one, is adjusted in place
when the book is split, every balance is adjusted once: the parts the tasks write do not overlap
accrue() does not return while any part of the book is still being adjusted
the two halves of a book that is split are adjusted at the same time, on two workers

origin.section: Subtasks Write Disjoint Ranges and Read Nothing Another Subtask Writes

concepts: Subtasks of an in-place action write disjoint ranges; an inclusive midpoint changes the boundary elements twice, the same ones every run.
invokeAll(left, right) forks one task, runs the other on the current thread and waits for the first, so the two halves run at once and a task can also do work after its subtasks are done.
A RecursiveAction's compute() must wait for its subtasks, as invokeAll does; forking them and returning lets invoke() return while the leaves are still writing.
